title: Morning GPU + Network priority bullets
content:
Quick morning scratchpad — mix of tasks, checks, and commands. Not a playbook; for my shift handoff and a place to dump sticky items.

Context:
- Observed transient egress saturation on cluster-gpu-03 over the last 36h. Appears correlated with model-pipeline burst during nightly batching window.
- Working hypothesis: simultaneous KV-cache warmups + backend fetches causing 95p egress spikes.
- Need short-term mitigation and a follow-up PR to routing/batching logic.

Top priorities (today)
- [P0] Stabilize cluster-gpu-03 network egress before lunch (11:30 PDT). If >600Mbps sustained, start mitigation plan.
- [P1] Run targeted netperf/iperf tests on node gpu-03a,b to confirm NIC-level vs host-level issue.
- [P1] Add temporary routing cap: limit concurrent external fetches from model-pipeline to 4 per host (config flag).
- [P2] Draft quick rollout note for the team: what we changed and rollback steps.

Immediate checklist (what I'll do now)
- Check alerts & short logs:
  - k get pods -n infra | grep gpu-03  # quick pod health
  - kubectl logs -n infra model-pipeline -l app=model-pipeline --since=2h | grep "fetch" | wc -l
- Network perf test (non-disruptive):
  - sudo apt-get install -y iperf3 || true
  - iperf3 -c 10.2.3.5 -t 10 -P 3  # run from gpu-03a to infra-net-1
  - iperf3 -s (on infra-net-1) and check for packet loss
- Collect nic counters:
  - ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_" > /tmp/eth0-stats.txt
  - sar -n DEV 1 10 (if installed)
- Reduce burst window (temporary):
  - update config: MODEL_PIPELINE_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES=4 (k8s configmap patch)
  - apply to model-pipeline service with canary (10% pods) first

Quick mitigation steps (if >600Mbps)
- Add iptables egress shaping on host (as temporary emergency):
  - tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 600mbit burst 32kbit latency 400ms
  - Note: will persist only until host reboot; good for immediate relief but not long-term.
- Move heavy KV warmup tasks to off-peak window (2:00–4:00am) — coordinate with SRE scheduler.

Notes for follow-up engineering work
- Investigate model-pipeline behavior: is it retrying or backoff missing during warmup? Ticket: JIRA-AP-3421.
- Add more granular egress telemetry per-pod (sflow or eBPF counters). Need proposal: cost estimate + retention.
- Look at kernel/NIC driver versions on affected nodes (possible regression after recent kernel update).

Handoff notes (for next shift)
- What I changed: applied configmap patch to reduce concurrent fetches; rolled out to 10% of model-pipeline pods at 10:45 PDT.
- What to watch: egress per-host (grafana: infra->network->egress-by-host), model-pipeline error-rate, pod restart count.
- If situation worsens: revert configmap by rolling patch to previous value and revert canary.

Meeting prep items (later today)
- 13:00 sync with SRE and model infra (15m): agenda — observed spikes, temporary mitigations, timeline for telemetry ship.
- 16:00 post-mortem draft (30m): gather logs, timeline, who touched what.

Loose ideas / brain-dump
- Could we pre-populate KV cache incrementally across hosts using staggered token assignment instead of simultaneous fanout? Explore token-based warmups.
- Consider adding per-tenant egress quotas to protect infra from single-customer batch jobs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: Is the egress pattern originating from model-pipeline or downstream image fetches? Need dnstap or flow log to confirm.
- Q2: Can we get 95p egress per-host into daily SLOs? Metric owner: @Zara.
- TODO: File infra RFC for per-host egress telemetry — assign to Samir (due EOW).

Reminders (personal)
- Ping legal about upcoming SOC2 notes for private deploy tests.
- Coffee before 11:00 or I will rant in the meeting.

Last-ditch rollback plan (if catastrophic)
- Scale down model-pipeline to zero replicas (kubectl scale) and gradually scale back with very low concurrency flag. Contact on-call before scaling to zero.

Log snippets to paste into ticket (examples)
- "2026-03-09T22:14:02Z model-pipeline fetch failed 503 retry=3 host=gpu-03a egress=720mbps"
- "iperf3 result: 0.9% packet loss, avg throughput 680Mbps between gpu-03a -> infra-net-1"

End of scratchpad — will update after tests complete.

-- Evan
